verdicts.note: The record holds the indicator as two paragraphs, as the page prints it. The 23 through 36 months cell on this page prints one more paragraph after the indicator paragraphs the record holds: a one-sentence inclusion note. The extraction left it out on purpose and the assignment says to report it, not to fail the record for it. It stands above the rule that separates the indicators from the examples, in the row the document's own key (page 30) labels as indicators, and it carries no "Note:" label. Here the note is about a child who is blind, and the same sentence stands in all three age columns.

Round 2, a second reading on the page image (page 115). The 23 through 36 months cell prints three paragraphs above the rule that separates indicators from examples, and the record now holds all three, in order. The added third span is that cell's own one-sentence inclusion sentence about a child who is blind. All three age columns print the same sentence; the span takes the third printing, which in the extractor's view follows directly on the second paragraph of the 23 through 36 months cell. Nothing from another column and nothing from the examples row is in the record. The foundation statement and the heading number are equal. The Summary and Limits now state the sentence as an allowance, with its two named senses kept as examples. The page gives the sentence no label; calling it a note is the pack's word and changes no condition.

Limits says learning a new word after one or two meetings "is stated as" understanding it, not saying it. The indicator's own verb there is wider than understanding; the reading rests on the foundation statement, which is about understanding. Not a contradiction, so confirmed.

Round 2, a second reading on the page image (page 120). The 23 through 36 months cell prints three paragraphs above the rule, and the record now holds all three, in order. The foundation statement and the heading number are equal. The Summary states the sentence as an allowance and keeps its three kinds of device as examples. Limits spells the abbreviation out: the expansion is printed on this page in the neighbouring column, not in this cell, and it is correct. Limits also says, truly, that the sentence does not say how the stated sentence length applies to a child who uses a device.

Summary, last clause: it says the child's answers stay on the subject "the other person raised". The indicator says only that the child responds to the other person on the same topic of the conversation, in general; it does not say who brought the topic up (the record's own Limits says as much, and the page's first example has the child start the topic). Drop the attribution. Wording, code and the correction are right: the page breaks the hyphenated compound at a line end in the indicator and prints it on one line in the foundation statement, so the restored hyphen is correct.
